title: Designing Detection
objective: Design secure paths for logging, detection, and notifications, and investigate insufficient evidence or false positives defensively.

sections.title: Defining the Observation Scope from Assets and Risks
paragraphs: Before adding more alarms, security personnel organize the accounts, data, public access paths, highly privileged principals, and critical operations that need protection. Detection requirements include not only what to detect, but also who will investigate and what information is needed to determine the scope of impact.

GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors, analyzes, and processes AWS data sources and logs. Because a GuardDuty finding does not establish a definitive cause, investigators correlate the target resource and time with primary evidence from activity history, the network, and the application, according to the type of finding.

sections.title: Connecting the evidence trail from change to detection
paragraphs: CloudTrail records actions performed by users, roles, and AWS services as events, supporting auditing, governance, and compliance. Define the organization, account, and Region scope, retention, encryption, and access permissions so that the operations, target resources, times, and principals needed for investigations are preserved. When investigating GetObject or PutObject for an important S3 bucket, select and record read and write data events for the target bucket in the CloudTrail trail. Management events and event history alone do not provide S3 object-level data events.

How to read the figure: Blue shows the delivery of management operations and selected data events through a configured CloudTrail trail; red shows GuardDuty findings generated by analysis of configured data sources; and purple shows an analyst investigating from a finding back to the original event. None of these is an application request path. Because a finding does not establish the cause, verify the actor, target, and time against primary evidence such as the original event. Do not broadly expose the protected, centralized archive or delete the original event based only on a finding.

S3 protection in GuardDuty independently analyzes S3 data events and produces findings. So that operations staff can investigate the original operation, separately select the target bucket’s data events in a CloudTrail trail and retain them as investigation logs.

sources.label: Enabling CloudTrail event logging for S3 buckets and objects

sections.title: Turn notifications into actionable detection findings
paragraphs: Alerts should include severity, target, time, basis for detection, related events, the responsible team, and criteria for deciding the initial response. If the same detection finding generates a large number of notifications unconditionally, critical signals can be buried. Therefore, define conditions for aggregating duplicates, prioritizing, escalating, and suppressing notifications.

Detection quality cannot be measured by simply counting how few notifications are generated. Review missed detections, false positives, the time required for investigation, and missing evidence, then improve the detection rules, data sources, and responder workflow.

sources.label: SCS-C03 Exam Guide: Detection and Logging

checkpoints.prompt: A security professional who manages multiple AWS accounts has enabled GuardDuty S3 Protection. When a finding for suspicious access is generated, they need to trace who performed GetObject or PutObject on which objects in important S3 buckets. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Store only the detection findings and delete the original operation history.
choices.explanation: You cannot verify the basis for the findings or their impact scope.

choices.text: Make all buckets public and eliminate the need for access logs.
choices.explanation: This loses the protection boundary and auditability.

choices.text: In the organization’s CloudTrail trail, select and record data events for GetObject and PutObject on critical S3 buckets, and retain them in a protected, aggregated archive. For GuardDuty findings, trace back to the principal, resource, time, and original event to verify the hypothesis.
choices.explanation: This links the primary evidence of S3 object operations to the findings, allowing investigation without concluding that a finding itself is the cause.

checkpoints.prompt: GuardDuty reported communication from an EC2 instance running the order API to a known suspicious IP address. No new AWS API operations were found during that period, but VPC Flow Logs are being collected for the relevant network interface. What should the security team examine first to determine the scope of the communication?

choices.text: Using the interface and timestamp from the finding, correlate the source, destination, ports, and whether the communication was allowed or rejected in the VPC Flow Logs.
choices.explanation: Because this finding concerns network communication, the relevant traffic can be checked in the corresponding flow logs. The logs alone do not establish whether the instance was compromised.

choices.text: Search only the CloudTrail management events from the same time and conclude that there was no communication if none are found.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail management events record AWS API operations. They do not show whether the EC2 instance sent network traffic.

choices.text: Based only on the IP address in the finding, conclude that all instances in the same VPC were compromised.
choices.explanation: A finding for one network interface does not reveal the status of other instances or whether their communications succeeded.

checkpoints.prompt: The security operations team is overwhelmed by too many notifications and is missing critical findings. Which improvement is most appropriate?

choices.explanation: Critical indicators will no longer be detected.

choices.text: indiscriminately increase the number of recipients by adding unrelated personnel.
choices.explanation: Responsibilities and priorities will become unclear.

choices.text: Define finding severity, duplicate aggregation, scope, ownership, escalation, and suppression conditions, then review missed findings and false positives.
choices.explanation: This can improve notifications so they are actionable.
